messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient, a 46-year-old male, was admitted in 2006 with a 3.7 mm skin cancer on his left forearm. He had multiple recurrences which were treated with surgical resections, topical imiquimod, and intra-tumour IL-2 as per protocol. The patient was enrolled in IMM-101-001 study which resulted in a decreased rate of new disease however his condition worsened with lung metastases developed. Subsequently, he received ipilimumab on a clinical trial which showed a remarkable response, with most of the lesions resolving and a couple of visceral lesions remaining stable over 5 years.  
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
CONDITION AT DISCHARGE:
Stable with no acute problems.

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
The patient is advised to follow up for further evaluation to monitor his health status. 

FOLLOW-UP RECOMMENDATIONS:
A follow-up with a specialist is recommended for ongoing care. 

MEDICATIONS:
None.

FUTURE TREATMENT PLAN:
To be decided upon specialist consultation. 

SUMMARY:
The patient, a 46-year-old male, was admitted with a 3.7 mm skin cancer on his left forearm that had recurred several times. He was treated with surgical resections, topical imiquimod and intra-tumour IL-2, however, his condition worsened and he was enrolled in a clinical trial. The patient received ipilimumab and had a remarkable response, with most of the lesions resolving and a couple of visceral lesions stable over 5 years. The patient will follow up with a specialist for ongoing care and treatment planning.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The 3.7 mm Breslow-thickness skin cancer treated with intralesional IL-2, an IMM-101 trial and ipilimumab is malignant melanoma of the skin of the forearm. It belongs to chapter C (neoplasms). The category is C43, malignant melanoma of skin.

CODE: C43
